name: Ola Finance
rootCause: Ola Finance on the Fuse chain published a blog post on the hacking incident, stating that the attack lost approximately $4.67 million, including 216,964.18 USDC, 507,216.68 BUSD, 200,000 fUSD, 550.45 WETH, 26.25 WBTC, and 1,240,000.00 FUSE. The attack uses a reentrancy vulnerability in the ERC677 token standard.

descriptions.text: Ola Finance on the Fuse chain published a blog post on the hacking incident, stating that the attack lost approximately $4.67 million, including 216,964.18 USDC, 507,216.68 BUSD, 200,000 fUSD, 550.45 WETH, 26.25 WBTC, and 1,240,000.00 FUSE. The attack uses a reentrancy vulnerability in the ERC677 token standard.

On March 31, 2022, Ola Finance's Fuse chain lending protocol was exploited via an ERC-677 reentrancy vulnerability, enabling repeated asset withdrawals within a single transaction. The attacker drained approximately $4.67 million in stablecoins, wrapped tokens, and FUSE by looping through pools before debts were properly recorded. The lending pool contracts permitted ERC-677 token transfers to invoke callbacks that reentered withdrawal logic before borrower debt and pool balances were updated. The contracts did not implement reentrancy guards or checks-effects-interactions ordering, exposing them to repeated withdrawals in a single transaction.
